episodes.152397: A potent storm system moved across the Ozarks which produced periods of heavy rainfall for portions of the region. Record rainfall occurred in West Plains on the 28th of the month with many other locations recording significant rainfall which lead to flooding of some creeks and streams.
episodes.152629: During the late evening of October 28th through the morning of October 29th, Tropical Storm Zeta swept rapidly across north Georgia producing widespread wind damage and isolated flooding across north and portions of central Georgia. Around 1.5 million customers lost electricity for some period of time, some for several days.
episodes.152752: A big gullywasher came on the 28th as the system in the Plains neared. Rain came down in buckets over the northern half of the state, with four to more than five inch amounts at several locations. This included Des Arc (Prairie County) and Harrison (Boone County). Three to four inch totals occurred at Booneville (Logan County), Batesville (Independence County), Gilbert (Searcy County), Jonesboro (Craighead County), Lead Hill (Boone County), Marshall (Searcy County), Mena (Polk County), Mountain Home (Baxter County), Newport (Jackson County).||In and around Little Rock (Pulaski County), there was spotty flash flooding. At Sherwood (Pulaski County), an inch and a half of rain dumped in twenty minutes. The Little Rock Air Force Base (Pulaski County) got 1.66 inches in an hour.||In a four day period ending at 600 am CST on the 30th, precipitation in parts of the north and west exceeded six inches. It was a complete reversal of fortune from the dryness experienced up until the deluge. For the month, rain was just under five inches above average at Harrison (Boone County).
episodes.152784: Heavy rain brought flooding to parts of northeast Arkansas at the end of October.
episodes.153190: Moisture associated with the remnants of Hurricane Zeta, combined with the approach of a strong 500 mb low from the Plains states, resulted in widespread heavy rainfall from 2 to 4 inches.
episodes.153191: Moisture associated with the remnants of Hurricane Zeta, combined with the approach of a strong 500 mb low from the Plains states, resulted in widespread heavy rainfall from 2 to 4 inches.
episodes.153193: Moisture associated with the remnants of Hurricane Zeta, combined with the approach of a strong 500 mb low from the Plains states, resulted in widespread heavy rainfall from 3 to 5 inches.
episodes.153213: Warm and moist conditions occurring ahead of an arriving cold front led to a band of showers capable of producing wind damage across southeast South Carolina.
episodes.153456: Widespread amounts of three to five inches of rainfall were observed across the mountains and foothills during the 24-hour period ending with the passage of Tropical Storm Zeta across the lower mid-Atlantic region.  Despite its rapid speed across the region, the storm brought two to three inches of rain across portions of Wilkes and Surry Counties during a single hour, resulting in widespread flooding of many creeks and streams.  The flooding was severe enough in some cases to wash out the bridges passing over these creeks.  Lesser flooding was observed elsewhere across the Highlands of North Carolina where the rainfall rates were not as intense.
episodes.153457: Tropical Storm Zeta passed quickly across the lower mid-Atlantic region on the morning of the 29th, but still brought 2-3 inches of rainfall to the foothills of the Blue Ridge and the Piedmont region.  Much of this rain fell within a 1-2 hour period, resulting in rapid flooding of several small streams.  Residual moisture in the wake of Zeta allowed for redevelopment of bands of slow-moving storms producing additional heavy rain, which also resulted in localized flooding across the Piedmont of Virginia.
episodes.153472: Hurricane Zeta made landfall in southeast Louisiana during the late afternoon hours of Wednesday, October 28th as a strong category 2 hurricane with maximum sustained winds of 110 mph. Zeta quickly raced northeast and moved across inland southeast Mississippi and inland southwest Alabama during the evening hours. Shortly after midnight, Thursday, October 29th, Zeta weakened to a tropical storm while moving across central Alabama. Since Zeta was moving at a rapid 25-30 mph across the area, it brought frequent hurricane force wind gusts and extensive wind damage to inland southeast Mississippi and inland southwest Alabama. Hurricane force gusts extended as far east as coastal Alabama, which contributed to a significant storm surge that impacted portions of Mobile and Baldwin Counties. Sustained minimal tropical storm force winds extended as far east as portions of the western Florida Panhandle.   ||Widespread tree and power line damage was reported across inland southeast Mississippi into inland southwest Alabama as these areas experienced sustained moderate to strong tropical storm force winds and frequent hurricane force wind gusts. Despite a lack of observations, peak gusts of 80 to 100 mph very likely occurred. In fact, the Mobile Regional Airport measured the highest wind gust in the local area of 91 mph. A station in Grove Hill measured a peak gust of 80 mph. Several counties in this area experienced near or 100% power outages. Many homes also suffered minor roof damage, with numerous homes suffering moderate to major damage, many of which were the result of trees falling onto homes.||The highest storm surge occurred in Mobile Bay, along the immediate shores of Baldwin County, as well as southern Mobile County along the Mississippi Sound, as well as Dauphin Island. Peak storm surge inundation was surveyed to be 7 to 9 feet across parts of Bayou La Batre and Coden, as well as the Baldwin County side of Mobile Bay from the Mobile Bay Causeway to south of Point Clear. A few isolated areas approached 10 feet. These higher water levels are a combination of storm surge and wave action. ||Flooding reports were isolated as the fast movement of the storm precluded excessive rainfall amounts. Rainfall totals of 3 to 6 inches were reported along and just to the right of the center across inland southeast Mississippi into inland southwest Alabama.  ||At the time of publication, there was not enough data available to calculate an estimate to storm total monetary damages. ||Here is a breakdown of the county impacts:||Stone County MS: The county experienced sustained tropical storm force winds with gusts of 80-100 mph, which resulted in significant tree and power line damage. Numerous to widespread power outages were reported. 170 homes were damaged, experiencing either roof damage or damage due to downed trees with 15 of the homes experiencing major damage. The most extensive damage was in the eastern portion of Stone County, which was impacted by the eastern eyewall.||George County MS: The county experienced sustained tropical storm force winds with frequent gusts of 80-100 MPH, resulting in widespread tree and power line damage throughout the county. Nearly 100% of the county was without power. Numerous homes suffered damage, mainly to roofs. Approximately 100 homes had major damage with 30 completely destroyed, due primarily to downed trees. There was one minor injury as an individual was in a car accident while trying to drive to work during the storm. A little over 8 million dollars in residential damage was estimated along with over 6.5 million in damages to the power infrastructure.||Perry County MS: The county experienced sustained strong tropical storm force winds with frequent gusts to hurricane force. This resulted in significant tree and power line damage. Numerous to widespread power outages were reported. 36 homes were damaged, experiencing either roof damage or damage due to downed trees.||Green County MS: The county experienced sustained tropical storm force winds with frequent gusts of 80-100 MPH which resulted in widespread tree and power line damage throughout the county. Power outages were near or at 100%. Numerous homes suffered damage, mainly to roofs. Approximately 30 homes had major damage with 7 destroyed, due primarily to downed trees.||Wayne County MS: The county experienced sustained tropical storm force winds resulting in significant tree and power line damage. Numerous power outages were reported. 13 homes were damaged, experiencing either roof damage or damage due to downed trees.||Mobile County AL: The county experienced sustained tropical storm force winds with gusts to hurricane force. Mobile Regional Airport had a peak gust of 91 MPH. It is likely that the northern portion of Mobile County experienced frequent gusts of 80-100 MPH close to where the core of Zeta moved through. These winds resulted in widespread downed trees and power outages to the central and northern part of the county, including the city of Citronelle. Numerous homes suffered roof damage and some were damaged due to downed trees. The extent of downed trees and power outages became more scattered further south. A significant storm surge occurred on the west end of Dauphin Island, Bayou La Batre, and Coden where a survey team measured peak inundation of 7 to 9 feet along the immediate coast. A few isolated areas approached 10 feet in Bayou La Batre and Coden. These higher water levels are a combination of storm surge and wave action. A storm surge with peak inundation of 4 to 6 feet was measured in the northwest portion of Mobile Bay, which impacted areas close to the coast along the bay. The Highway 90 causeway was completely flooded and water was reported on a part of Water Street in Downtown Mobile. ||Baldwin County AL: Tropical Storm force winds impacted much of Baldwin County with frequent gusts of 60 to 70 mph. These winds resulted in scattered down trees and power outages. Some homes also experienced minor roof damage. A significant storm surge impacted the eastern shore of Baldwin County. A survey team measured peak inundation of 7 to 9 feet in northeast Mobile Bay along the Highway 90 causeway and south along the Eastern Shore from Daphne to Point Clear. These higher water levels are a combination of storm surge and wave action. Several piers were destroyed on the Eastern Shore and the seawall at the Fairhope Pier was damaged. A few boats docked at the small marina at the Fairhope Pier were sunk. Damage also occurred to a few of the parks along the immediate shoreline. Significant surge also extended south to Point Clear where surge went across County Road 1.||Washington County AL: Sustained tropical storm force winds with frequent gusts of 80 to 100 mph resulted in widespread tree and power line damage throughout the county. Power outages were near or at 100%. Numerous homes suffered damage, mainly to roofs or fallen trees.||Choctaw County AL: Tropical Storm force winds resulted in scattered down trees and power outages. One mobile home in Butler suffered major damage due to a tree that fell on it. 3 mobile homes further south had minor damage. Approximately 3500 customers lost power.||Clarke County AL: Sustained strong tropical storm force winds with frequent gusts of 80-90 mph resulted in widespread tree and power line damage throughout the county. Power outages were near or at 100%. Over 250 power poles and 150 transformers had to be replaced. Numerous homes suffered damage, mainly to roofs. Over a thousand homes were damaged, with approximately 25 suffering major damage or destroyed, due primarily to downed trees.||Wilcox County AL: Sustained tropical storm force winds with frequent gusts of 80 to 90 mph resulted in widespread tree and powerline damage throughout the county. Power outages were near or at 100%. Numerous homes suffered damage, mainly to roofs. At least 100 homes had moderate to major damage, due primarily to downed trees.||Monroe County AL: Strong tropical storm force winds with gusts to hurricane force resulted in numerous to widespread downed trees and powerlines. Significant power outages were reported. Damage to numerous structures, including buildings in downtown Monroeville.||Conecuh County AL: Strong tropical storm force winds resulted in numerous to widespread downed trees and powerlines. A significant number of power outages were reported.||Butler County AL: Tropical storm force winds downed trees and powerlines. Numerous power outages were reported. Some homes were damaged due to downed trees.||Crenshaw County AL: Tropical storm force winds downed trees and powerlines. Numerous power outages were reported. Some structures were damaged due to downed trees.||Covington County AL: Tropical storm force wind gusts downed some trees in the county.||Escambia County AL: Tropical storm force winds downed trees and powerlines. Some power outages were reported.||Escambia County FL: Tropical storm force winds, primarily in frequent gusts, resulted in the downing of some trees and scattered to numerous power outages.||Santa Rosa County FL: Tropical storm force wind gusts resulted in the downing of some trees and scattered power outages. No structural damage was reported.||Okaloosa County FL: Tropical storm force wind gusts occurred. However, no significant damage was reported.
episodes.153775: Tropical moisture streamed into the area as the remnants of Zeta approached and interacted with a stalled frontal boundary. A prolonged period of heavy rain led to flooding across portions of Northern Virginia.
episodes.153776: Tropical moisture streamed into the area as the remnants of Zeta approached and interacted with a stalled frontal boundary. A prolonged period of heavy rain led to flooding across portions of central and southern Maryland.
episodes.153836: Low pressure combined with the remnants of Tropical Cyclone Zeta tracking across the Middle Atlantic region produced heavy rain across portions of Central Virginia and the Virginia Northern Neck.
episodes.153837: Low pressure combined with the remnants of Tropical Cyclone Zeta tracking across the Middle Atlantic region produced heavy rain across portions of the Lower Maryland Eastern Shore.
episodes.153851: Tropical moisture and heavy rain overspread western North Carolina throughout the 28th through the morning of the 29th as the center of Tropical Storm Zeta moved quickly from the mouth of the Mississippi River into the southern Appalachians. Strong winds developed across portions of western North Carolina during the morning, downing hundreds of trees across the area. Multiple trees fell on structures and vehicles. Upslope flow into the Blue Ridge escarpment enhanced rainfall rates such that widespread totals of 3 to 5 with locally higher amounts inches occurred over about a 24 hour period. This resulted in development of flash flooding across portions of the southern mountains and northern foothills.
episodes.153855: Winds associated with Tropical Storm Zeta caused damage throughout northwestern NC. Wind gusts reached 30-40 knots during the peak of the storm. Numerous trees were blown down by Tropical Storm Zeta, with dozens falling on homes, power lines or blocking roadways, and thousands reportedly losing power.
episodes.153859: Winds associated with Tropical Storm Zeta caused damage and power outages in southwestern Virginia, concentrated close to border with North Carolina. Wind gusts reached 30-40 knots during the peak of the storm. Numerous trees were blown down by Tropical Storm Zeta, with many falling on homes, power lines, and blocking roadways. A thunderstorm closely following Zeta contributed to some of the wind damage.

The Cooperative Weather Observer at Concord 4SSW (CONV2) recorded a 24-hour rainfall measurement ending at 7am EDT on October 30th of 3.80 inches. This was the third highest 1-day rainfall measurement during the month of October for this station since it was opened in September 1950. It is also the 13th highest 1-day measurement of any month for this station.

The Cooperative Weather Observer at Appomattox (APXV2) recorded a 24-hour rainfall measurement ending at 7am EDT on October 30th of 3.99 inches. This was the second highest 1-day rainfall measurement during the month of October for this station since it was opened in November 1937.

The Cooperative Weather Observer at Buckingham (BUKV2) recorded a 24-hour rainfall measurement ending at 7am EDT on October 30th of 3.54 inches. This was the fourth highest 1-day rainfall measurement during the month of October for this station since it was opened in May 1894.

The Cooperative Weather Observer at Altavista (ALTV2) recorded a 24-hour rainfall measurement ending at 7am EDT on October 30th of 3.56 inches. This was the fourth highest 1-day rainfall measurement during the month of October for this station since it was opened in May 1945.
State Highway T was closed due to flooding at Possum Walk Creek.
State Highway 95 was closed at Bryant Creek due to flooding.
State Highway EE was closed at the North Fork River due to flooding.

Stream gauges reported flash flooding developed along the major headwater streams in Transylvania County after 4 to 5 inches of rain fell across much of the southern and western part of the county in around 24 hours. The Little River overflowed its banks and flooded Merrill Rd in the eastern part of the county. The French Broad River inundated multiple roads in the Rosman area, including Depot St, where some homes has to be evacuated, as well as Hannah Ford Rd, E Main St, and Highway 178. The Davidson River also overflowed its banks in the Pisgah Forest area, flooding portions of Davidson River Rd and Wilson Rd, and indicating backwater flooding of Turkey Creek which inundated Deavor Rd.

Emergency manager reported flash flooding developed along portions of the Catawba River and many of its tributaries across central McDowell County after 3 to 5 inches of rain fell in around 24 hours. In addition to around two dozen roads being inundated and closed, a water rescue occurred at an apartment complex in Old Fort when Mill Creek overflowed its banks. Private bridges were destroyed by intense stream flow along Second Broad River at Mimosa Dr and Clear Creek Rd (both in the Marion area) and along Peppers Creek Rd in North Cove. A culvert under Hidden Forest Drive was also washed out by a tributary of Limekiln Creek in Woodlawn. Additionally, a stream gauge on the Catawba River exceeded its established flood stage in the Pleasant Gardens community, indicating inundation of a campground off North Main St just north of Marion.
State Highway 181 was closed at Bryant Creek due to flooding.
Numerous roads were flooded across Posey County. Two water rescues were conducted, both on roads that frequently flood.

Pappy's Trading Post published photos to their social media site of their property and nearby areas inundated by the Nottely River. The USGS river gage downstream reported the Nottely River rose to Minor Flood Stage, cresting at 14.68 feet. Radar estimates indicate that 4 to 6 inches of rain occurred in the area, resulting in the flash flooding.
Highway FF at Hunter Creek was closed due to flooding at the low water crossing for several hours.
Highway Y was closed at Cowskin Creek due to flooding of the low water crossing.
Highway U at Bryant Creek was closed due to flooding of the low water crossing.

Extensive flooding took place along Cub Creek during the late morning and afternoon hours as two to three inches of rain fell across the basin with the passage of Tropical Storm Zeta, most of it within a one hour period, on top of an additional one to two inches that fell during the previous evening for a total of nearly five inches in 24 hours.  Virtually all of Cub Creek Park was flooded, and the bridge on South Bridge Street that crosses the creek was completely over-topped by the flooded creek.  Elsewhere, the dam of a 3.5 acre pond collapsed at around 1:40 pm EST, sending flood water that washed out at 20 foot section of Woodfield Way just downstream.  Concern for the bridge on Industrial Park Road that crosses the creek about one mile downstream prompted evacuations of multiple businesses and apartments that would be cut off if the that bridge too was washed out, though it did not. Country Club Extension Road along Little Cub Creek was flooded and closed, as was Westover Road, where storage buildings and nearby residences were also flooded.

Extensive flooding took place along Moravian Creek during the late morning and afternoon hours as 2 to 3 inches of rain fell across this basin with the passage of Tropical Storm Zeta, most of it within a 1-hour period.  This rain was in addition to another 1 to 2 inches that fell during the previous evening, for a total of nearly 5 inches in 24 hours.  Newspaper reports indicate that nearly all of Moravian Creek was out of its banks, causing flooding Wilkes Community College's lower campus.  School Street further downstream was also closed by the flood waters.

Numerous businesses along Wilkesboro Boulevard from the Yadkin River bridge to Memorial Park were flooded when the Yadkin River swiftly rose out of its banks, the result of 4 to 5 inches or rain within a 24-hour period both preceding and during the passage of Tropical Storm Zeta. Multiple personal weather stations observed 2-3 inches of rain within a 1-hour period just before the onset of flooding. Flash flooding ended as the river crested during mid-afternoon, and roads were reopened during the evening once the river receded. Among the businesses flooded were Extreme Collision Auto Body, which had to move several vehicles to prevent them from being damaged by flood waters. Flood waters completely inundated Memorial Park as well as the Yadkin River Greenway.

The Reddies River at Wilkesboro (REDN7) crested at 11.79 feet (6760 cfs), which was between a 5- and 10-year Annual Return Interval per USGS StreamStats.  These rises were the result of 3-5 inches of rainfall within a 24-hour period, much of which fell within a 2-hour period during the passage of Tropical Storm Zeta.  The rapid rises resulted in the precautionary evacuation of residents from the Rose Glen Manor assisted living facility, though flooding did not enter the buildings.  Employees of other nearby businesses were evacuated as well out of precaution.

Widespread flooding took place along Fishing Creek during the late morning and afternoon hours as 2 to 3 inches of rain fell across this basin with the passage of Tropical Storm Zeta, most of it within a 1-hour period. This rain was in addition to another 1 to 2 inches that fell during the previous evening, for a total of nearly 5 inches in 24 hours. Newspaper reports indicate that Fishing Creek Arbor Road at Fishing Creek was washed out when the culvert running beneath the road failed.  Further downstream, flood waters from the creek carried away several dozen propane gas storage tanks.  It is unclear how many tanks were recovered and still functioning. In addition, high water rescues were conducted for cars that became stranded in the flood waters.  One rescue was conducted on Highway 115 near the intersection with Speedway Road, and the other was on Speedway Road near the Fishing Creek Road intersection.

Moravian Creek quickly rose out of its banks during the passage of Tropical Storm Zeta, the result of three to five inches of rain within a 24-hour period.  This caused several roads intersecting the creek to be flooded and closed until the flood water receded, including Germantown Road and Falls Road near the Moravian Falls waterfall.
Flooding due to heavy rain caused by Tropical Storm Zeta resulted in flooding along the Middle Fork of the Reddies River.  Colvard Road was flooded and closed for several hours as a result.

Heavy rain across central and western Wilkes County due to the passage of Tropical Storm Zeta caused rapid river rises along the Yadkin River.  The Yadkin River quickly rose out of its banks, flooding multiple roads in the Roaring River and Ronda communities, including Red, White and Blue Road, Roaring River Road and Clingman Road.

Emergency manager and stream gauges indicated flash flooding developed along the Johns River and Yadkin River basins after 3 to 5 inches of rain fell across much of Caldwell County in about 24 hours. Johns River flooded multiple roads in the Collettsville area, including Highway 90 and Valley View Circle. Water from the Yadkin inundated several roads in the Happy Valley community, including Yadkin River Rd and Indian Grave Rd.

A stream gauge on Mud Creek in Hendersonville indicated flash flooding occurred after 2 to 4 inches of rain fell across the area in around 24 hours. Several low lying spots along the creek were inundated. Additionally, Wash Creek flooded a parking lot and access road at the intersection of S Church St and S Main St.

Reports of 2 to 2.5 inches of rain caused rapid river rises along the South Fork of the New River.  At least one low bridge was flooded along Boggs Road, making the bridge impassible for several hours.
Highway H at the North Fork River was closed due to flooding at the low water crossing.
Highway NN at Rocky Creek was closed due to flooding at the low water crossing.
Around two inches of rain during a 2-hour period caused flooding of Powder Mill Creek onto both School Board Road, while flooding of Doe run closed both Doe Run Road and Ashpone Road.
Two trees were brought down across a roadway in Pinnacle.

Between 2 and 4 inches of rainfall occurred in the hours before and during the passage of Tropical Storm Zeta. Multiple personal weather stations indicate that more than half of the rain fell within a 2-hour period as the center of the storm passed. The heavy rain caused widespread flooding of small creeks and streams, pushing many out of their banks. Several roads, both within the Elkin community and the surrounding area, were flooded and impassible until flooding receded, including Commerce Street, Pleasant Hill Road, and Memorial Park Drive. A debris flow was reported on Johnson Ridge Road.

Multiple weather stations in the vicinity of the Blue Ridge in Carroll County indicate that between 1.5 and 2.5 inches of rain fell inside a two-hour period during the passage of Tropical Storm Zeta at rates of one to two inches per hour in spots.  This rain caused multiple streams to flood out of their banks onto nearby roadways, making them impassible until the water receded, including across Spring Bud Road and Route 52 as Paul's Creek rose out of its banks.

Privately-owned weather stations across northern Ashe County indicate that 1.5 to slightly over 2 inches of rain fell across soils already very moist from rainfall earlier in the past 24 hours.  This caused flooding of Helton Creek, overflowing across a bridge along Jim Duvall Road.

Multiple privately-owned weather stations indicate that between 2 and 2.5 inches of rain fell during the passage of Tropical Storm Zeta.  Soils were already very moist due to rounds of rain that passed across the region earlier in the night.  Runoff from the rain caused Cranberry Creek to overflow its banks across a bridge on Double Springs Church Road, making the bridge impassible for several hours.

Multiple weather stations in the southeastern portion of Franklin County recorded between two to locally 3.5 inches of rainfall inside a three hour period during the passage of Tropical Storm Zeta.  Rainfall rates of one to two inches per hour were observed in some locations.  This rain caused multiple streams to flood out of their banks onto nearby roadways in the Snow Creek area, making them impassible until the water receded.  This includes Muddy Fork Road flooded by Reed Creek and Sutton Hollow Road closed due to flooding of Crawford Creek and Snow Creek. Fawndale Road and portions of the Virgil Goode Highway were also reported flooded and impassible for a few hours.
Heavy rain during the passage of Tropical Storm Zeta caused a debris flow along Highway 16.
Old Courthouse was closed at Besley Road due to flooding on Wolftrap Creek.
Two trees were blown down by thunderstorm winds.
Two roads flooded in the northern part of Pittsylvania county where up to three inches of rain fell from Tropical Cyclone Zeta. The roads were closed until the water receded.
Thunderstorm winds brought down a tree.

Multiple data sources across all of Patrick County, including trained spotters and personal automated weather stations, indicate that between two and locally three inches of rain fell during a two-hour period during the passage of Tropical Storm Zeta from roughly 9 am to 11 am EDT.  Rainfall rates were observed at one to two inches per hour in spots.  This rain caused multiple streams to flood out of their banks onto nearby roadways, some up to 12 inches deep in the vicinity of Buffalo Creek, making them impassible until the water receded.  This included Egg Farm Road where it intersected Grassy Branch Creek, as water was estimated to be at least eight inches deep over the roadway.

Heavy rain from Tropical Storm Zeta caused Whittier Creek to overflow its banks and completely wash out Nurse Road, making the road impassible.  Water was estimated to be flowing about two feet over the bridge before it was destroyed.

Between two and four inches of rainfall occurred in the hours before and during the passage of Tropical Storm Zeta.  Multiple personal weather stations indicate that more than half of the rain fell within a 2-hour period as the center of the storm passed. The heavy rain caused widespread flooding of small creeks and streams, pushing many out of their banks.  Several roads, both within the Ararat community and the surrounding area, were flooded and impassible until flooding receded.  A few bridges were damaged or destroyed.

events.narrative: Two swift-water rescues were performed for the occupants of vehicles that became stranded where Hiatt Road passes across Stoney Creek.  The road was flooded and impassible for several hours.  This flooding was the result of heavy rain which occurred during the passage of Tropical Storm Zeta.

Emergency manager and stream gauges indicated flash flooding developed along tributaries of the Catawba River, including Johns River and Lower Creek after 3 to 5 inches fell across the area in around 24 hours. Johns River inundated multiple roads, including Johns River Loop and Johns River Rd. A water rescue occurred on Johns River Loop. Lower Creek also flooded Antioch Rd near Highway 18. Pax Hill Rd and Hartland Rd also flooded in the Chesterfield community.
A couple trees were uprooted or snapped near Eden. In addition, a roof was blown off of a building.

A tributary of Daniels Creek overflowed its banks and flooded onto Oakland Drive, making it impassible until the water receded.  The flooding was the result of up to two inches of rain inside a two hour window, with one to 1.5 inch per hour rainfall rates per nearby personal weather station observations.
A few trees were blown down near downtown Danville, with one blocking the intersection of Kirk and Seminole Drive, and another blocking the intersection of West Main Street and Virginia Avenue.
Heavy rain caused by Tropical Storm Zeta caused a debris flow across Highway 268, partially blocking the road.

Between two and four inches of rainfall occurred in the hours before and during the passage of Tropical Storm Zeta. The heavy rain caused widespread flooding of small creeks and streams, pushing many out of their banks. Several roads, both within the Dobson community and the surrounding area, were flooded and impassible until flooding receded. A few bridges were damaged or destroyed. Highway 601 was impassible due to flooding of Bear Creek, where one swift water rescue was performed for an automobile that became stranded in the flood waters.  Fisher River Park was also closed due to flooding.

Accotink Creek at Strathmeade Springs was in Minor Flood stage during the indicated period, reaching a peak level of 252.38 feet at 11:30 AM on October 29th. Woodburn Road was covered by over a foot of water at its lowest point.

Several roads were observed flooded and closed in and around the community of Jonesville. Among them, over six inches of water from the nearby Yadkin River was observed flowing rapidly over Fabric Lane.
Jones Mill Road was closed due to flooding between Spicers Mill Road and Constitution Highway.
Old Office Road was closed due to flooding between Zoar Road and Burr Hill Road.

Bassett Branch overflowed its banks and flooded onto Meadowood Trail, making it impassible until the water receded. The flooding was the result of up to two inches of rain inside a two hour window, with one to 1.5 inch per hour rainfall rates per nearby personal weather station observations.
Woodburn Road was closed due to flooding between Spicewood Drive and Robey Avenue, due to Accotink Creek rising out of its banks.

Although heavy rainfall tapered off across the French Broad basin during the morning of the 29th, flooding continued along the Little River in response to continued runoff. Minor river flooding also developed along the French Broad in the Blantyre area during this time and continued into the early morning hours of November 1st.

Difficult Run at Wolf Trap was in Minor Flood Stage during the indicated time period, reaching a peak level of 195.64 feet at 6:05 PM on October 29th. Just over a foot of water covered Brown's Mill Road at its lowest point.
Several roads were closed due to flooding in the Madison and Criglersville areas.

Although heavy rain tapered off across Caldwell County during the morning, stream gauges indicated continued runoff from the heavy rain resulted in high water conditions persisting along Johns River as well as Lower Creek in Lenoir through the afternoon. Multiple roads remained inundated, particularly in the Collettsville areas.

The Yadkin River at Wilkesboro (WKSN7) crested within minor flood stage at 15.86 feet (13,100 cfs), resulting from heavy rain during the passage of Tropical Storm Zeta.  This crest is between a 2-year and a 5-year annual return interval per USGS StreamStats.  The crest would likely have been higher had W. Kerr Scott Reservoir not reduced its outflow by 500 cfs in response to the flooding at several points downstream.  By holding back outflow and combined with heavy inflow, W. Kerr Scott Reservoir had risen to a pool stage of 1044 feet by 9 pm on October 29th, up 14 feet from before the onset of rainfall during the day prior.
